picks.title: Four Friendly Facts by Kanshin Allison Tait
picks.summary: This Dharma talk explores the Four Noble Truths through Robert Thurman’s playful framing of the “Four Friendly Fun Facts.” Looking at suffering as something to understand rather than escape, the talk considers how self-centeredness creates alienation, how compassion reconnects us with others, and how the Eightfold Path offers a practical way to work with our lives as they actually are. Along the way, it touches on impermanence, Tonglen practice, and approaching Buddhist practice as an ongoing experiment in wisdom and compassion.Books mentioned: Wisdom Is Bliss: Four Friendly Fun Facts That Can
picks.reason: Dharma talk on Four Noble Truths, suffering, compassion, and the Eightfold Path in Zen.

picks.title: Ep. 10: Nico and Devon Hase — This Messy Gorgeous Love (Practising the Dharma in real relationships)
picks.summary: In this episode of Living Dharma, co-hosts Tsunma Kunsang Palmo and Justin Kelley welcome Nico and Devon Hase, husband-and-wife Buddhist teachers and authors who write about what happens when lofty ideals meet the rub of ordinary life. Their answer begins with getting real. picks.reason: Buddhist teachers discuss applying Dharma ideals in real-life relationships.

picks.title: Sitting With Your Karma
picks.summary: Given at a One-Day Sitting at the Boulder Zen Center, this talk picks up a question left open in the previous episode, "Sitting Like a Buddha." If zazen is not a means to awakening but its enactment, what about karma? Thoughts, fragments of story, and small triggers of dissatisfaction keep arriving, and we assume awakening means their absence. The talk proposes instead that we are always sitting and living with our karma; what changes is our relationship to it. Karma means intentional action, and the talk reads intention as a leaning: every action leaves a trace, the trace becomes a dispositio
picks.reason: Zen talk on karma and awakening, focusing on relationship to intentional actions.

picks.showTitle: Zen Stories & Buddhist Teachings for Sleep by Midnight Monk
picks.title: You Don't Have To Fix Everything… Fall Asleep to Gentle Zen Stories & Buddhist Teachings for Rest
picks.summary: Tonight, we explore the possibility that life does not need to be finished before we are allowed to rest. Through Buddhist wisdom, Zen stories, and gentle reflection, this long-form sleep episode looks at the pressure to improve, resolve, prepare, and become, and what can change when that pressure begins to soften.This is a quiet journey through mindfulness, letting go, self-compassion, acceptance, craving, effort, and the search for inner peace. Rather than asking you to fix your thoughts or reach a particular state, the episode invites a different relationship with whatever is already here:
picks.reason: Zen stories and Buddhist teachings guide gentle mindfulness and acceptance for rest.

picks.title: Enjoy the Dharma! by Kanshin Allison Tait
picks.summary: What does it mean to truly enjoy Zen practice? In this talk, Kanshan explores joy, presence, and the meaning of practicing without a “gaining idea.” Drawing on Suzuki Roshi and Zenkei Blanche Hartman, he reflects on our tendency to think something is missing or wrong with us, and how Zen invites us instead to meet this life with greater openness, balance, love, and joy.------Kanshin Allison Tait - 09/06/26 - Suggested Donation $5
picks.reason: Talk on joy, presence, and practicing Zen without attachment to gain.

picks.title: The Sage: 15 Minute Guided Meditation

picks.reason: Reflection on Dhammapada chapter about spiritual friendship and training the mind.

picks.reason: Discusses spiritual awakening and identity dissolution with references to Zen and consciousness.
